title: ops-feedback-kiteboard-notes-2026-08-09
body:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis of recent ops and CS threads (internal ticket samplings from July 2026) condensed into a small set of cohort lenses and candidate fixes. The goal: produce 3–5 actionable, low-risk patches we can ship in a 2-week cycle, plus one middling-risk project for Q3. Framing metaphor: 'kiteboard' = lightweight surface fixes that let the product ride stronger winds (usage spikes) with minimal engineering drag.

Data sources reviewed:
- 72 CS tickets from 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31 (sampled across tiers).
- Three customer calls with platform/infra teams (enterprise: fintech, healthtech, marketplace).
- Observability traces for failed inference fallbacks during peak hours (hosting regions: us-west-2 + eu-west-1).
- Internal heatmap exported from CS tooling (see linked Confluence page).

High-level themes (cohort lenses):
1) Small-batch latency cliffs for short chat sessions (cohort: PLG devs > 10k monthly calls).
   - Pattern: requests with short prompts + frequent stop sequences see 30–80ms extra per-token on average during concurrent bursts.
   - Quote: "When we spin up a new test suite, latency spikes and dev experience stalls." — dev lead, startup client.

2) Confusing model-fallback behavior for dedicated customers (cohort: Dedicated customers with pinned versions).
   - Pattern: client pin to v1.2 but fallback silently to quantized variant during resource shortage; output style changes cause UI regression.
   - Quote: "The tone shifted and our generated answers stopped matching our tests — we didn't know a fallback happened." — platform engineer, enterprise.

3) Embedding consistency drift across regions (cohort: multi-region customers using similarity search).
   - Pattern: embedding vectors from eu vs us show small offset due to differing model variants and sequence-length truncation; results in lower recall for cross-region queries.
   - Quote: "We see different top-k results by region — makes global search unpredictable." — search infra owner.

4) Onboarding docs mismatch for API streaming + function-calls (cohort: new integrations, first 2 weeks after signup).
   - Pattern: quickstarts show sync examples; streaming behavior and reconnect guidance under-documented leading to repeated CS tickets.

Candidate kiteboard patches (low-effort, high-impact):
A) Short-session batching hint + client-side sample code (owner: DevX, est 3 dev days)
   - What: add a per-request hint/flag to prefer single-request micro-batching optimization and provide client SDK snippet.
   - Why: addresses Theme 1 by reducing batching misclassification and improving cold-start latency for short chats.
   - KPIs: median p50 latency for <200-token sessions, number of latency-related tickets.

B) Explicit fallback header in responses + docs update (owner: Serving Runtime + Product Docs, est 2 dev days + 0.5 docs)
   - What: include X-Redwood-Fallback: true|variant in response headers when runtime substitutes model variant due to capacity.
   - Why: addresses Theme 2, reduces surprise changes in application behavior and gives customers signal to trigger alerts/telemetry.
   - KPI: reduction in "mystery drift" tickets and fewer rollback requests.

C) Embedding region-consistency note + opt-in normalizer (owner: Optimize team, est 4 dev days)
   - What: document the known regional variant differences and ship an opt-in post-processing normalizer (simple zero-mean normalization + token-window alignment) for customers using multi-region similarity.
   - Why: quick mitigation for Theme 3 while longer-term model alignment is planned.
   - KPI: improvement in cross-region recall in customer testbeds.

D) Streaming quickstart refresh + reconnect recipe (owner: DevX Docs + Console, est 1.5 days)
   - What: rewrite streaming examples to show reconnect/backpressure patterns, include sample tests for function-calling + streaming.
   - Why: reduces repetitive onboarding tickets (Theme 4) and lowers first-contact CS time-to-resolution.

Medium-effort proposal (Q3):
E) Model-fallback customer-visible policy UI (owner: Console product + Serving Runtime, est 4–6 sprints cross-team)
   - What: Console toggle and policy editor allowing Dedicated customers to set strict vs permissive fallback behaviors, plus alerting rules when fallbacks occur.
   - Why: longer-term solution to Theme 2; reduces customer surprise and aligns with enterprise SLAs.

Quick heuristics for triage (how we mapped tickets to patches):
- Ticket severity buckets: P0 (production outage), P1 (data/regression in production behavior), P2 (developer experience/friction). We focused on P1/P2 for kiteboard patches.
- Cross-checks: each candidate patch was validated against at least two distinct customers or one enterprise + telemetry.

Risks & unknowns:
- Fallback header might expose internal variant metadata customers use incorrectly; mitigate by publishing guidance and limiting detail to variant family rather than internal hashes.
- Embedding normalizer might mask real model-drift issues; make opt-in and provide a diagnostic report.
- Short-session hint could interact with autoscaling heuristics — require load-test in staging focusing on micro-batching behavior.

Immediate next steps (two-week sprint plan):
Week 1:
- DevX: implement and land streaming quickstart refresh (D).
- Serving Runtime: spike on response-header change and minimal server-side hook (B).
- Optimize: prototype embedding normalizer on a small test corpus (C).
- CS: prepare two customer follow-ups to validate expectations (A/B customers for B and C).
Week 2:
- Land header change behind feature flag + docs (B) and ship DevX quickstart (D).
- If prototype shows promise, deploy embedding normalizer as opt-in in staging (C).
- Create a small SDK snippet and PR for short-session batching hint (A) as a follow-on patch to land in sprint+1.

Who to loop in now:
- @Liam Chen (observability) — load-test plan and telemetry hooks.
- @Marina Ortega (product) — approval for header visibility and console messaging.
- @Aisha Khan (SRE) — staging rollout for header and micro-batching experiments.
- Sales CS reps for two pilot customers (listed on Confluence page).

Appendix: sample verbatim snippets from tickets (redacted)
- "We pinned 1.2 but suddenly started getting shorter replies — our CI failed because outputs changed mid-run." — enterprise ticket #CS-4478
- "Our similarity layer returns different top results depending on where the query hits — makes caching useless." — mid-market client note
- "The streaming example didn't show how to reconnect on network hiccup, we had to invent it." — PLG integration note

Minimal acceptance criteria for shipping patches: 
- Header: feature-flagged, documented, and applied in staging with a smoke test showing header present on fallback cases.
- Docs: streaming quickstart live and linked from onboarding email.
- Embedding normalizer: shipped behind opt-in with a diagnostic report and migration notes.

Open questions for leadership:
- Do we want to expose fallback reasons beyond a boolean (risk vs transparency)?
- Prioritization: land three kiteboard patches this cycle or focus on header+streaming only?

Notes to self: keep kiteboard naming for follow-ups to signal low-cost, quick iterations. This doc is intentionally compact — if we get a green light I will expand an engineering RFC for the header change with API examples.

Document history:
- Drafted 2026-08-09 by Asha Patel
- Added telemetry notes + KPIs 2026-08-11 (Liam Chen)
- Revised risks and sprint plan 2026-08-12 (Marina Ortega)
